q: 1. Another aim of e-procurement is increased choice of supplier leading to sourcing items:
explain: answer in book is C As per scribid E-procurement widens the pool of accessible suppliers online, so buyers can source items from the right source among a broader supplier base.

q: 2. Public works must be of very good quality, because
options: it is paid in higher rate
users are general public and maintenance is not timely difficulty and costly
explain: But as per book b. Public works serve the general public continuously; poor quality causes costly, delayed maintenance affecting many users, so high quality is essential.

q: 3. The construction of airports is treated as
explain: Airports involve large-scale earthwork, runways, and infrastructure comparable to dams/highways, classifying them as heavy construction.

q: 4. Which of the following is not a PERT event?
explain: An event is a point in time (start/finish of an activity), not a continuing process. 'Class is being attended' is an ongoing activity, not an instantaneous event.

q: 5. When used in connection with the progress of a work, the term amount indicates the
options: total expenditure on a particular item
value of the finished product in a manufacturing operation
explain: In progress reporting, 'amount' refers to the total expenditure incurred on a particular item of work.

q: 6. The first stage of a large construction work to
explain: Every construction project begins with the conception of the idea before design, study, or contracting can occur.

q: 7. The conception of idea for any construction work is the responsibility of
explain: The owner identifies the need and originates the idea for a construction project; engineers and contractors act on it afterward.

q: 8. The field of activities of an engineer includes
options: approval of construction plans by the local authority
inspection and payment of work done by contractor
explain: An engineer's role spans estimation, plan approval liaison, and inspection/certification of contractor's work - covering all listed activities.

q: 9. The contractor is responsible for
options: procuring material which is not supplied by the owner
organizing and planning the work as per drawing
executing the work as per specifications laid down in the contract
explain: A contractor's overall responsibility covers material procurement (where not owner-supplied), planning, and execution per specifications - all of the above.

q: 10. The process of calculating the resource requirement of a project is known as
explain: Resource aggregation is the specific technique of summing up resource requirements period-wise across all activities of a project.

q: 11. The chart which gives an estimate about the amount of materials handling between various work stations is known as
explain: A travel chart (from-to chart) quantifies material movement/handling volume between different work stations.

q: 12. The bar chart is also known as
explain: Bar charts were developed by Henry Gantt and are universally known as Gantt charts.

q: 13. In the analysis of rate, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: In standard rate analysis practice, contractor's profit margin is conventionally taken as 15% of the cost.

q: 14. The prime input of material planning is
explain: Material planning primarily depends on forecasting the demand for materials required over the project duration.

q: 15. A milestone chart
options: shows the inter dependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: A milestone chart displays key events in the order they are expected chronologically, without necessarily depicting logical activity dependencies as a network would.

q: 16. Milestone chart is an improvement over
explain: Milestone charts evolved to overcome the limitation of simple bar charts by marking key milestones, thus improving upon bar charts.

q: 17. A Gantt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual process with the scheduled progress
explain: A Gantt/bar chart plots planned vs actual progress bars, allowing direct comparison between scheduled and actual performance.

q: 18. The jobs going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: Gantt charts visually show progress bars extending beyond the planned bar length, conveniently indicating jobs ahead of schedule.

q: 19. The earliest method used for planning of projects was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart), developed in the early 1900s, predates CPM and PERT (developed in the 1950s) as a project planning tool.

q: 20. Actual performance of task is called
explain: An activity represents the actual performance of a task that consumes time and resources.

q: 21. An activity is
options: the beginning or end of a specified job
an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the progress of work up to a certain limit
explain: An activity is defined as an identifiable element of work within a project that consumes time and resources.

q: 22. CPM requires
explain: CPM (Critical Path Method) uses a single deterministic time estimate for each activity.

q: 23. PERT requires
explain: PERT uses three time estimates - optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic - for each activity to account for uncertainty.

q: 24. The optimistic time represents the
options: shortest possible time in which an activity can be completed if everything goes exceptionally well
time in which the activity is normally expected to complete under normal contingencies
time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty
explain: Optimistic time (to) is the minimum time an activity could take assuming ideal conditions with no complications.

q: 25. The time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty, is called
explain: Pessimistic time (tp) is the maximum time an activity would take under unfavorable/difficult conditions.

q: 26. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: the office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' describes a state/point in time (an event), not an ongoing process consuming time and resources like the other options.

q: 27. In the network shown in Fig., the concurrent and preceding activities corresponding to activity 2-4 are respectively
explain: From the given network diagram, activity 2-3 runs concurrently with 2-4 (both starting from node 2), while 1-2 precedes it - matching answer key option b.

q: 28. Dummy activities are use to
explain: Dummy activities (zero duration, shown dotted) are used purely to preserve correct logical dependencies and maintain proper network sequencing.

q: 29. A project is
options: a large dam constructed across a river for a single or multi-purpose
any job involving many people and large money
a work of major importance involving huge men and material
an organized team work to achieve a set task within the time limit
explain: A project is generally defined as an organized, coordinated effort of a team to accomplish a specific objective within a defined time frame.

q: 30. Which of the following is a weakness of bar chart?
explain: Bar charts fail to clearly show activity interdependencies, cannot represent uncertainties, and give limited insight beyond basic progress - all are weaknesses.

q: 31. Slack time refers to
explain: Slack time is associated with events (in PERT terminology) - the allowable time an event can be delayed.

q: 32. An event is
options: the start and/or finish of an activity or the group of activities
explain: An event marks the start and/or finish point of one or more activities; it is instantaneous and consumes no time.

q: 33. Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A bar chart plots activities against time, with bar length representing the duration of each activity.

q: 34. Policy is
options: a rule or a set of rules never to be violated
a definite route along which one has to proceed
a procedure for preparing the project report
a set of broad guidelines stipulated by management
explain: Policy refers to broad guidelines set by management to direct decision-making, distinct from rigid rules or fixed procedures.

q: 35. An activity requires
explain: An activity, by definition, is work that consumes both time and resources (manpower, material, equipment).

q: 36. Critical path method is an effective and powerful method of assessing
options: What tasks must be carried out
Where parallel activities can be performed
The shortest time in which you can complete a project
explain: CPM identifies required tasks, parallel activity opportunities, and the minimum project duration - covering all listed aspects.

q: 37. Select the correct statement.
options: Activity arrows in a CPM network are drawn to scale
The tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
Arrow head represents the start of an activity
explain: None of the given statements is correct: arrows are not drawn to scale, the tail represents the start (not finish), and the head represents the finish (not start) of an activity.

q: 38. Monitoring of a construction project is done
explain: Monitoring is an ongoing activity carried out throughout the project implementation (execution) period to track actual vs planned progress.

q: 39. PERT is an abbreviation for
options: pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Program (Programme) Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 40. CPM stands for
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method, a network-based project scheduling technique.

q: 41. PERT is
explain: PERT networks are built around events (milestones) connecting activities, making PERT event-oriented.

q: 42. CPM is
explain: CPM networks emphasize activities (jobs) and their durations, making CPM activity-oriented.

q: 43. PERT adopts
explain: PERT uses probability distributions (three time estimates) to account for uncertainty in activity durations, making it probabilistic.

q: 44. CPM adopts
explain: CPM uses a single fixed time estimate per activity, making it a deterministic approach.

q: 45. Which of the following statements is true?
options: PERT is activity oriented and adopts deterministic approach
CPM is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
CPM is activity oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
PERT is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
explain: PERT is indeed event-oriented and uses a probabilistic approach (three time estimates), correctly combining both characteristics unlike the other options.

q: 46. Which of the following is an example of parallel activities?
options: construction of walls and casting of roof
construction of walls and carpentry work of doors and windows
casting of roof and construction of parapet wall
digging of well and construction of septic tank
explain: Wall construction and carpentry (doors/windows) work can proceed simultaneously without one depending on completion of the other, making them parallel activities.

q: 47. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The head event marks the completion (ending point) of an activity in a network diagram.

q: 48. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its
explain: The tail event marks the starting point of an activity in a network diagram.

q: 49. A dual role event
options: is the head event as well as a tail event
is the beginning of one event and the end of another
is any event other than the initial and final events
explain: A dual role event simultaneously serves as the head (completion) event of preceding activities and the tail (start) event of succeeding activities.

q: 50. A dummy activity
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a fictitious link (zero duration, zero resource) used only to maintain logical sequencing between real activities.

q: 51. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges, it results in an error called
explain: Dangling occurs when an event (other than the final one) has no succeeding activity emerging from it, leaving it disconnected from the rest of the network.

q: 52. If the path of activities leads back into itself, the resulting error in the network is known as
explain: Looping is the network logic error where a sequence of activities forms a closed loop, violating the forward-progress requirement of a network.

q: 53. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are;
explain: A probability factor (Z) of zero corresponds to the mean of the normal distribution, giving a 50% chance of completing within scheduled time.

q: 54. In PERT, the critical path represents the
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the initial to final event
ideal path by proceeding along which the project can be completed as per schedule
path which takes into account the completion of the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is defined as the longest path through the network from start to finish, determining minimum project duration.

q: 55. Negative float for any activity means that the activity is:
explain: Negative float indicates the activity is behind schedule beyond what the project allows, making it super-critical (worse than critical).

q: 56. Area under beta distribution curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time (mean of the beta distribution) divides the area under the probability distribution curve into two equal halves.

q: 57. Negative slack indicates
explain: Negative slack means the required schedule time is less than available time is not met - i.e., the activity/event is running behind the desired schedule.

q: 58. Contractor's prequalification is required for
explain: Prequalification is generally required only for major and specified/specialized works to ensure the contractor has adequate capacity and experience.

q: 59. Which of the following terminology is not relevant to a CPM planning?
explain: Optimistic time is a PERT term (part of the three-estimate approach), not used in CPM which relies on single deterministic durations.

q: 60. Actual performance of a task is called
explain: An activity represents the actual performance of work/task in a project.

q: 61. Zero float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Zero float (zero slack) means the activity has no spare time and lies exactly on the critical path, making it critical.

q: 62. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Positive float indicates the activity has spare time available and can be delayed without affecting the project, making it sub-critical.

q: 63. The total float for any activity along the critical path in CPM is
explain: By definition, activities on the critical path have zero total float, as any delay directly delays project completion.

q: 64. Direct cost of project is due to
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages to labour
explain: Direct costs are those directly attributable to the execution of work, such as material costs and labour wages.

q: 65. Total project cost
options: initially reduces and then increases with increase in time
initially increases and then reduces with increase in time
explain: As project duration increases from crash time, direct cost falls while indirect cost rises; the combined total cost initially decreases then increases, forming a U-shaped curve.

q: 66. The total cost versus time curve is
explain: The sum of direct and indirect cost curves against project duration forms a U-shaped curve with a minimum at the optimum duration.

q: 67. Crashing to the project means
options: reducing the time of completion by spending more resources
reducing the cost of project by delaying the time of completion
reducing the project size to save the resources
explain: Crashing means shortening the project completion time by applying additional resources (at extra cost) to critical activities.
